Eventos como la pérdida de empleo, deudas perdonadas o retirar dinero de un fondo de jubilación pudieran tener un impacto tributario. Si sus ingresos han disminuido, usted podría ser elegible por primera vez para ciertos créditos tributarios, tales como el Crédito Tributario por Ingreso del Trabajo. Lo más importante es que si usted cree que pudiera tener dificultades para pagar sus cuentas tributarias comuníquese inmediatamente con el IRS. Hay medidas que podemos tomar para ayudarle a reducir la carga. Además, usted debería presentar su declaración de impuestos a tiempo aunque no pueda pagar para evitar multas adicionales. pages.description: The comment is an apparent swipe at Benjamin Netanyahu and Donald Trump, who both face elections in coming weeks.
pages.text: Macron accuses foreign leaders of exploiting French riots for political gain Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters Macron accuses foreign leaders of exploiting French riots 21 October 2026 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Patrick Jackson , Marco Silva and Thomas Copeland , BBC Verify AFP via Getty Images Protesters rallied in Lille along with other cities across the country French President Emmanuel Macron has accused foreign leaders of exploiting the riots which erupted across the country on Saturday for electoral purposes. Without naming them, he said they were campaigning for forthcoming elections "at France's expense" with their comments on the violence, which erupted on the fringe of cost-of-living protests. Speaking on a visit to the Middle East, he referred to them as "leaders who are in campaign mode, whether here in the region or on the other side of the Atlantic". It was an apparent swipe at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces parliamentary elections next week, and US President Donald Trump, for whom mid-term polls fall next month. Making a Better Battery Credit: Raw Pixel/Pixabay Helping smartphones hold their charge longer. Light-weight and energy-efficient, lithium-ion batteries have long been the battery of choice for powering smartphones, laptops, hoverboards, drones and other portable electronic devices. But even these low-maintenance batteries have their drawbacks—they lose their ability to hold charge after about 3 years, can catch on fire and often have to be recharged daily. To make a better lithium-ion battery or find innovative alternatives, PML researchers in collaboration with scientists from the Material Measurement Laboratory (MML) are studying how lithium batteries behave on some of the tiniest of scales, a few tens of atoms across. The scientists use an instrument that injects with exquisite precision an ultranarrow beam of lithium ions (charged atoms of lithium) into the negative terminal of a laboratory battery. Customs officials said the 45-year-old Mexican firefighter had looked "conspicuously nervous" as he tried to go through the green - nothing to declare - exit at the airport. They conducted a drugs test on the man - which came back positive for cocaine - before proceeding to check his suitcase. They did not find any drugs, but vipers, rattlesnakes and other species of snakes and lizards, including iguanas, hidden in shampoo and cream bottles, plastic containers and balls of socks. "My colleagues at the airport are used to a lot when it comes to souvenirs in suitcases, but we've never had 37 live venomous snakes and 55 lizards from Mexico before," said Jens Ahland, spokesman for the Cologne Customs office. Some were being kept "in inhumane conditions", Ahland said. Others had died during the journey from Mexico City via Istanbul. Paula Abreu Pita Manga are Japanese comic books and graphic novels. They are typically written and illustrated by a single person, known as mangaka . They are usually printed in black and white and read right-to-left. And they are incredibly popular, in Japan and beyond. When Frederik L. Schodt, author of Manga! Manga! Until then, for me, OpenStreetMap was just the group we’d formed in Mexico out of the legendary Rancho Electrónico, Mexico City’s hackerspace. During those days, I discovered it was so much more: a regional community, with faces, stories, perspectives, and generosity. I understood why these in-person gatherings matter so much. Marcos Gonzales Harsha Marcos serves as the Principal Deputy Director at the U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE's) Office of Technology Commercialization (OTC). pages.text: Mario Balotelli: Why always him? The rise and fall of the Italian striker - BBC Sport By Jess Anderson BBC Sport journalist Maverick. Loose cannon. Unmanageable. Mario Balotelli heard it all. Perhaps better known for off-field antics than his undeniable - yet arguably wasted - talent with the ball at his feet, the Italian has always attracted headlines. Fifteen years have passed since his famous 'Why always me?' Manchester derby T-shirt celebration, which came just days after a firework was set off in his own bathroom, causing a house fire. The 36-year-old is still playing, now in the United Arab Emirates first division with Al-Ittifaq alongside his biological brother, Enock Barwuah. Here, BBC Sport looks at a career that has included 13 clubs, six countries - and an assist for arguably the most famous goal in Premier League history. Mancini to Mourinho - cracks begin to show Typical of his unconventional footballing life, Balotelli's career did not begin in an elite club's academy. Instead, by his mid-teens he was turning out for Italian third-tier side Lumezzane, close to the family home in Concesio. A trial at Barcelona did not lead to a long-term stay, and instead he was picked up by Inter Milan in 2006. It was at Inter that Balotelli first came across his great mentor - Roberto Mancini. The relationship between the two has been likened to that of a father and son. Under the Italian coach's tutelage, Balotelli flourished. pages.text: Mary Anning: The forgotten fossil hunter who transformed Britain’s Jurassic Coast | National Geographic HISTORY & CULTURE WOMEN'S HISTORY MONTH The forgotten fossil hunter who transformed Britain’s Jurassic Coast Mary Anning and her most important dinosaur finds went unsung, but her legacy now draws travelers to southwest England. London‘s Natural History Museum displays several of Mary Anning‘s remarkable fossil finds, including this one of an ichthyosaur (lower). Photograph by Tommy Trenchard, Panos Pictures/Redux By Cathy Newman Published March 29, 2021 • 11 min read If you had lived in Victorian times, you’d have spotted her, perhaps, at the foot of Church Cliff to the east of Lyme Regis, a seaside town on England’s southwest coast. She’d have a wicker basket in one hand, a small geologist’s hammer in the other, and be dressed in a plaid coat and cape made of heavy wool—it is chilly by the shore. Her small dog, Tray, would have been skittering by her side. Self-taught paleontologist Mary Anning would search for fossils along the Dorset coast, accompanied by her dog, Tray. Photograph by GL Archive, Alamy Stock Photo What you might not have known then is that Mary Anning was arguably the greatest fossil hunter of them all, “the princess of paleontology,” a contemporary called her. In Victorian England, in an era of amateur scientists, fossil hunters were nearly always men. Anning was born in Lyme Regis, which sits on one of the great fossil deposits from the Jurassic era. Vicenzi Masks Under the Microscope Viewed under a microscope, mask fabrics are complex, varied and beautiful. By: Rich Press March 9, 2021 Facebook Linkedin X.com Email To understand how something works, it helps to see it up close. A team of researchers took this approach when studying the fabric masks that people wear to slow the spread of COVID-19. Those masks work by blocking some of the virus-filled droplets and smaller particles, called aerosols, that an infected person exhales, and they also offer some protection to the wearer by filtering incoming air. The researchers wanted to know how well different fabrics filter out those particles and what makes some fabrics better filters than others. Their research indicates that that cotton fabrics tend to perform better than synthetics , with cotton flannels being particularly effective. After being exposed to the moisture in a person’s breath, cotton fabrics perform better still . pages.text: Math Standards Math Standards Skip Navigation Math Standards The U.S. Census Bureau’s Statistics in Schools (SIS) activities are based on relevant education standards and guidelines that outline the foundational knowledge and skills students should have at certain levels. The SIS activities — which are designed to supplement or guide, not replace, existing curricula — help develop these skills and knowledge. Not all educators use the same standards. For this reason, many of the activities address multiple standards and guidelines. MATHEMATICS Common Core State Standards for Mathematics and for Mathematical Practice SIS activities reflect both the Common Core State Standards for Mathematics and the Common Core State Standards for Mathematical Practice. The Common Core State Standards for Mathematics are for grades K-12. Standards for kindergarten through eighth grade are organized by grade level; standards for grades nine through 12 are organized by topic, such as statistics and probability. The eight Common Core State Standards for Mathematical Practice are not tied to specific grade levels or topics. These practice standards represent various “habits of mind” that mathematics educators should seek to develop in their students. The practices rest on “processes and proficiencies” with long-standing importance in mathematics education. WEIRD & WILD Meet 'Hellboy': New Spiky-Headed Dinosaur Found A Triceratops cousin unearthed in Canada is so elaborately adorned "it blows your mind," one paleontologist says. By Devin Powell Published June 4, 2015 • 4 min read Triceratops has a new cousin with a devilishly good nickname: "Hellboy." Paleontologists who excavated the fossil skull of the horned beast from a steep cliff in Canada had a hell of time chipping the 600-pound (270-kilogram) specimen from the hard rock—hence its pet name. Only after freeing the fossil did the crew discover the moniker's pop culture connection. "There are these really stubby horns over the eyes that match up with the comic book character Hellboy ," says study leader Caleb Brown , a paleontologist at the Royal Tyrrell Museum of Palaeontology in Alberta, Canada. Though it had much smaller horns on its brow than its iconic cousin, the newfound dinosaur boasted a sizable horn on its snout and a fabulous frill on its head. (Also see " New Big-Nosed Horned Dinosaur Found in Utah .") The frill, or bony head protrusion, of Regaliceratops is so elaborate it "blows your mind," one scientist says. This week's guests remind us not only of the well-documented ways that Cuba revolutionized that gift, but also how it blossomed in South America. Chilean tenor saxophonist Melissa Aldana and Cuban pianist Gonzalo Rubalcaba stopped by after their recent Tiny Desk performance to chat about their own personal histories with jazz and its lineage in their respective countries. The memories Rubalcaba shares about Havana's jazz scene in the 1980s adds another layer to a story we've talked a lot about on Alt.Latino. And Aldana looks back on her youth learning music from her father and grandfather, both of whom were Chilean jazz pioneers. The conversation also covers the music they played at the Tiny Desk, which comes from their recent album, 'Filin,' a reexamination of a Cuban musical movement that lasted from the 1940s through the '60s. Ultimately, this week's episode is time spent with two master musicians to hear how their lives and experiences contribute to their mutual appreciation and love of jazz. Memorandum of Understanding Between EPA and OSHA for Implementation of TSCA Section 6 In December 2024, EPA and the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) of the U.S. Department of Labor entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) formalizing their coordination on EPA’s work to assess and manage existing chemicals under section 6 of the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA). EPA and OSHA anticipate that better coordination under this MOU will result in improved workplace health and safety protections for workers using existing chemical substances under TSCA and the Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Act and allow for effective implementation of national workplace and environmental protection statutes. Mentor-Protégé Program The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE's) Office of Small Business Programs (OSBP) manages the DOE's Mentor-Protégé Program (MPP). By developing long-term business relationships between small businesses and DOE prime contractors, the program helps increase the overall number of small businesses that receive DOE prime contracts and subcontracts. It operates separately from the Small Business Administration’s (SBA's) Mentor Protégé Program (All Small MPP). The DOE MPP encourages the Department's prime contractors to assist small disadvantaged businesses (SDB) certified by SBA under section 8(a) of the Small Business Act (8(a)), other small disadvantaged businesses, women-owned small businesses, service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, veteran-owned small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, historically black colleges and universities, and other minority institutions of higher learning to enhance their capabilities and improve their abilities to perform contracts and subcontracts for the DOE and other Federal agencies.
